transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They keep slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody else keeps telling me it's just regular notices they put on the doors, but... I know what's really happening.
Do you hear voices when no one else is around?
No, I don't hear any voices or anything like that. It's just... I just know what they're doing with the notes. But nobody is talking to me when I'm by myself.
Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or irritable?
No, not really. I haven't noticed feeling high or... or irritable. I don't get wound up like that. I'm just trying to mind my own business, mostly.
Have you been feeling depressed معظم اليوم nearly every day?

Yeah, pretty much every day. Most mornings I just... I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor. And it just kind of stays with me.
Do you feel that you deserve this because you’ve done something wrong?

No, I... I don't think I did anything wrong. I mean, I'm not a bad person or anything. I don't feel like I'm being punished. It's just... I just feel low all the time, but it's not because I feel guilty about something I did.
How long have you believed that the people at your apartment are watching you and sending notes about you?
Well, I guess... those thoughts about the neighbors and the office people watching me, sending those notes... it's been going on for about a year and a month now.
Did these beliefs about your neighbors start only after you became depressed?

Well, no, not exactly. I mean, the depression has been there a lot, but... there was a spell of several weeks where I was actually eating a bit better. I wasn't waking up feeling so hopeless every single morning. But even during that time, when my mood lifted a little, I still knew the neighbors were watching my door and reporting on me. That part never stopped.
Have you found yourself talking much less than you used to?
No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I don't go out of my way to talk to people much anyway, but I don't think I'm talking any less than normal when I do.
Have you been diagnosed with any brain or nerve condition?
No, I haven't. Um... I've never had a doctor tell me I have any kind of brain problem or nerve condition. Nothing like that.
Have you lost motivation to do everyday things?
No, not really. I mean, I still get up and do what I need to do around the house. I wouldn't say I've lost the drive to do everyday things, no.
Do you ever feel that your thoughts are being controlled by someone or something outside of you?
No, I can't say I've ever felt like that. My thoughts are my own. I don't feel like anybody or anything else is pulling the strings up there, if that's what you mean.
Have you found that your emotions feel flat or less expressive than they used to?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I still feel things pretty much the way I always have. I haven't noticed my emotions feeling flat or anything like that.
Do you ever feel that outside forces are trying to put thoughts into your mind?
No, nothing like that. Like I was saying a minute ago, my thoughts are just my own. I don't have any outside forces or anyone trying to put things in my head.
Has there ever been a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day?

Yeah, I'd say so. It's been going on for a lot longer than two weeks, really. Most mornings I just wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling inside. It's like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor. And that feeling just kind of stays with me pretty much the whole day.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I used to really look forward to things. Like choir practice, playing bridge, cooking a pot of beans on Sundays... even just doing little repair jobs for folks. But now, I mostly just let the phone ring. I just tell myself there's no point in going or doing any of it anymore.
For at least one month, have you believed that your neighbors were watching you and sending notes about you?

Yeah, that's actually the main reason I came in. I just know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They keep slipping notes about me to the front office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just standard notices taped to the doors, but I know what they're really doing.
Has there ever been a full month when you still believed your neighbors were watching you, but you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah, there was. A while back, there was a spell of several weeks where... well, I was actually eating a bit better, and I wasn't waking up feeling so hopeless every single morning. The heavy feeling kind of lifted for a bit. But even then, I still knew the neighbors were watching my door. I still knew they were reporting on me to the office. That never stopped, even when my mood was better.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?
No, I can't say I have. I've never seen anything that wasn't really there, or anything like that. It's just the stuff with the neighbors I told you about.
Since these beliefs started, has your ability to manage work, daily responsibilities, or relationships clearly gotten worse?

Yeah, it definitely has. I've... well, I've fallen behind on my bills, and I keep missing appointments. I actually stopped showing up for church and the volunteer work I used to do, too. It's just getting too hard to keep my days organized. And honestly, I just don't trust ordinary interactions with people anymore, not with everything going on. So, yeah, my day-to-day life has definitely taken a hit.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

Yeah, I've heard that a few times. People say they can't follow what I'm saying. Like, I'll try to explain something... I'll start talking about the rent, and then I'll mention the marina, and then the choir robes, and the wires in the walls. And they just look at me like I skipped half the story. I guess it all connects in my head, but it doesn't come out right for them.
